$comment: Run once in each new git worktree Roxy creates for a session.
A worktree is a fresh checkout: git only materializes tracked files, so
node_modules is EMPTY and any untracked .env is absent. Without this, the
first thing an agent does in a new workstream is discover that tsc reports
'Cannot use JSX unless the --jsx flag is provided' on every file, because
the base tsconfig it extends lives in node_modules.
npm ci (not install) so the lockfile is honoured exactly, and
--prefer-offline so it comes from the local npm cache: ~30s rather than a
cold network install.
Deliberately NOT a junction/symlink to the main checkout's node_modules.
It looks free (0.02s vs 30s) and it is a trap: writes go THROUGH a junction
to the real directory, so one workstream running an install or a native
rebuild mutates every other session's dependencies -- destroying exactly the
isolation worktrees exist to provide. 30 seconds is worth not debugging that.
npm ci alone is NOT enough: it fetches better-sqlite3's prebuilt binary
for the ABI of whichever plain node ran it (127 for node 22), while the app
loads it under Electron (130). The install then reports exit 0 and the
worktree is broken anyway -- 'npm run smoke:app' dies with ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED
/ NODE_MODULE_VERSION on a checkout that looks perfectly healthy. So setup
runs the worktree:setup script, which chains electron-builder's
install-app-deps to rebuild native modules against Electron's ABI (~8s,
idempotent).
Invoked via 'npm run' rather than inlined here because the setup command is
executed by PowerShell 5.1 on Windows, which has no '&&' operator; npm runs
its scripts through cmd.exe/sh, where the chain works on every platform.
Available: ROXY_PROJECT_ROOT, ROXY_WORKTREE_PATH, ROXY_PORT.
